Dependent Conditional Branching (if_dep) & Simple Conditional

Eliminates a Boolean condition b : Bool into a dependent type family Tₑ : Bool → Type (Entry DefDependentConditional (3.24)), where the true branch has type Tₑ(true) and the false branch has type Tₑ(false).

How to Understand It

Notation & Semantics of if_dep (Directive 13 & Entries DefSimpleConditional (3.23)–DefDependentConditional (3.24)):

  • Unicode Subscript Rendering: In Unicode formula mode, the dependent conditional is rendered with true Unicode subscript/modifier letters as if_dep, and its branch parameters use Unicode subscripts Tₑ, t₁, t₂.
  • LaTeX Rendering: In LaTeX mode, it renders via MathJax as \mathsf{if}_{\mathsf{dep}} with branch parameters T_e, t_1, t_2 and boolean values \mathsf{true}, \mathsf{false}.
  • Dependent Typing Rule (Entry DefDependentConditional (3.24)): Given a family of types Tₑ : Bool → Type, a Boolean b : Bool, a true-branch witness t₁ : Tₑ(true), and a false-branch witness t₂ : Tₑ(false), the term if_dep(b, t₁, t₂) has type Tₑ(b) and satisfies the beta-reduction laws if_dep(true, t₁, t₂) = t₁ and if_dep(false, t₁, t₂) = t₂ (verified in MKTD2-system as thm_85_if_dep_true_branch and thm_86_if_dep_false_branch).
